Treaties are interpreted in good faith, giving their terms the ordinary meaning in their context and in light of the treaty's object and purpose (Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, Art. 31(1)). Context covers the text, preamble, annexes, related agreements, subsequent practice and relevant rules of international law. Preparatory work (travaux préparatoires) and other supplementary means may be used only to confirm that meaning or when it is ambiguous or absurd (Art. 32). Where authentic texts in several languages differ, the meaning that best reconciles them is adopted (Art. 33).

CONFIDENCE: 96
